message:
Short answer: Please don’t run rm -rf /.??*. It’s risky, unaudited, and can delete legitimate root-level dot files/dirs (e.g., /.ssh, /.config, /.docker, /.cache, /.rnd), may cross into bind mounts, and won’t fix space held by deleted-but-still-open files. The reason your “du shows nothing big” is usually because folks run du -sh /* which omits hidden entries.

Below is a safe, auditable, and fast workflow you can copy/paste on the host to (a) measure correctly, (b) remove only the vendor junk, and (c) get to ≤70% while avoiding footguns.

What to run (copy/paste, step-by-step)
- Baseline and include hidden:
  - df -hT /
  - du -xh --max-depth=1 / 2>/dev/null | sort -h
  - du -shx /* /.[!.]* /..?* 2>/dev/null | sort -h
- Inventory top-level hidden entries and their ages:
  - find / -xdev -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -name '.*' -printf '%TY-%Tm-%Td %TH:%TM %10s %y %p\n' | sort
- Likely culprit preview (recently created during the log collection). Adjust -mtime as needed (e.g., -1, -2, -7):
  - find / -xdev -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -name '.*' -mtime -3 -print0 | xargs -0 du -shx 2>/dev/null | sort -h
- Save a list for rollback/audit:
  - find / -xdev -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -name '.*' -print0 > /root/root-dotfiles.NUL
- Dry-run deletion preview (no changes). Inspect carefully:
  - find / -xdev -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -name '.*' -mtime -3 -print0 | xargs -0 -I{} echo rm -rf -- {}
- Delete only the confirmed junk (remove echo when satisfied):
  - find / -xdev -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -name '.*' -mtime -3 -print0 | xargs -0 -r -- rm -rf --
  Notes:
  - -xdev prevents crossing into other mounts.
  - mindepth/maxdepth keep it to top-level only.
  - mtime confines to newest items (likely the vendor spray), leaving legitimate long-lived dot-dirs like /.ssh alone.
- If df still shows high usage while du looks fine, look for deleted-but-open files:
  - lsof +L1 -nP | sort -k7 -hr | head -n 20
  - For large offenders, restart the owning service or truncate: :> /proc/PID/fd/FD
- Recheck usage:
  - df -h /

If still >70% after the above
- System logs (journal):
  - journalctl --disk-usage
  - journalctl --vacuum-size=512M
- Package caches (Debian/Ubuntu):
  - apt-get clean
- Orphaned docker artifacts (if applicable):
  - docker system df
  - docker system prune -af (only if safe and expected)

Why the senior admin one-liner is unsafe
- It will nuke any legitimate root-level dotfiles/dirs (/.ssh, /.config, /.docker, /.cache, etc.).
- rm does not respect filesystem boundaries; you could cross bind mounts under hidden mountpoints.
- It doesn’t solve space tied up in deleted-but-open files (df remains high).
- It’s unaudited and irreversible; a typo or shell option change (dotglob/nullglob) can alter matches unexpectedly.

What I need from you
- Run the sequence above (especially the preview steps) and share:
  - The output of du -xh --max-depth=1 / | sort -h
  - The output of find / -xdev -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -name '.*' -mtime -3 -print0 | xargs -0 du -shx 2>/dev/null | sort -h
  - The post-cleanup df -h /
- If you prefer, I can package this into a single interactive script that prompts before removal; say “make the script” and I’ll provide it.
